diagnostic_evidence.quote: By stationarity, there exist $\lambda_i, \mu_i \ge 0$ with $\lambda_i u_i = 0$ and $\mu_i(u_i - C_{k(i)}) = 0$ such that
Applying complementary slackness yields the characterization in Table~\ref{tab:kkt}.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated conventions (lambda_i >= 0 with lambda_i u_i = 0 for the lower bound; mu_i >= 0 with mu_i(u_i - C_{k(i)}) = 0 for the upper bound), the Lagrangian stationarity condition is G_i - s_i*rho = lambda_i - mu_i, not mu_i - lambda_i. Taken at face value, complementary slackness yields the reverse of Table tab:kkt (e.g., alpha_k = 0 would force tau_k >= -rho, and alpha_k = C_k would force tau_k <= -rho). The written system is even inconsistent: for N = 1, Omega = [1], y_1 = 100, epsilon = 10, C = 1 with the optimum alpha_1 = alpha_1* = 0, it demands rho >= -90 and rho <= -110 simultaneously, so no valid multiplier exists (the correct system gives rho in [-110, -90], i.e., -rho in [90, 110]).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap lambda_i and mu_i in eq:kkt-stationarity (write G_i - s_i*rho = lambda_i - mu_i with the stated complementary-slackness conditions), which makes the derivation of Table tab:kkt valid; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The presented derivation of the KKT characterization (Table tab:kkt) is invalid as written; a reader using eq:kkt-stationarity literally obtains optimality conditions opposite to those the rest of the paper relies on for working-set selection, shrinking, and bias recovery. Since the table itself is correct and everything downstream uses the table, no downstream result is invalidated once the equation is corrected.
issues.title: KKT stationarity equation swaps the bound multipliers, contradicting Table 1
issues.why_classification: A forced one-symbol correction restores the derivation; the table, the MVP rule, the shrinking criteria, the bias recovery, and Algorithm 1 are unaffected, so no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{free}} = \emptyset$ at convergence (all support vectors lie exactly on a bound), \eqref{eq:bias-avg} is undefined.

issues.failure_explanation: At an optimal solution the KKT conditions give tau_i <= -rho for every i in Iup and tau_j >= -rho for every j in Idown, so the correct bracketing is tau_{i*} = max_{Iup} tau <= -rho <= min_{Idown} tau = tau_{j*}. Equation eq:bias-bounds asserts the opposite chain, which at convergence forces tau_{i*} >= tau_{j*} and fails whenever the bracketing interval is non-degenerate. Concrete instance: N = 1, Omega = [1], y_1 = 100, epsilon = 10 with the optimum alpha_1 = alpha_1* = 0 (so S_free is empty, Iup = {1}, Idown = {N+1}); there tau_1 = 90, tau_{N+1} = 110 and -rho lies in [90, 110], so the asserted chain 90 >= -rho >= 110 is impossible. The midpoint formula eq:bias-midpoint is symmetric in the two endpoints and remains valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the inequality chain in eq:bias-bounds to tau_{i*} <= -rho <= tau_{j*} (equivalently, state that -rho lies between tau_{i*} and tau_{j*}), leaving the midpoint formula unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the stated direction of the bound on -rho in the no-free-support-vector fallback is wrong; the midpoint convention, the bias-recovery line of Algorithm alg:smo, and all other guarantees are unaffected.
issues.title: Degenerate-bias remark reverses the KKT bracketing of -rho at convergence
issues.why_classification: A forced local reversal of two inequality signs; the correction withdraws no substantive promise, and no downstream claim, rate, or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the symmetric-kernel variant (m2) with $a = +1$, $P \succeq 0$ is preserved and the same guarantees apply.
The same solver applies to the symmetric-kernel variant (m2) by replacing $\Omega$ with $\Omega_s = \tfrac{1}{2}(\Omega + a\Omega^*)$~\cite{Espinoza2005}.

issues.failure_explanation: The premise is false: Omega* = [K(x_k, -x_l)] is not positive semi-definite in general. For the RBF kernel with antipodal training points x_1 = a, x_2 = -a (a != 0), Omega* = [[exp(-4*gamma*|a|^2), 1], [1, exp(-4*gamma*|a|^2)]] has determinant exp(-8*gamma*|a|^2) - 1 < 0, so it is indefinite. The conclusion also fails for general kernels: for a non-even PSD kernel, Omega_s = (1/2)(Omega + Omega*) can be symmetric yet indefinite (e.g., a feature-map construction with phi(1) = e_1, phi(-1) = 2*e_2, phi(2) = 2*e_1, phi(-2) = e_2 and training points {1, -2} yields Omega_s = (1/2)[[1, 2], [2, 1]], which has a negative eigenvalue), and for non-even kernels Omega_s need not even be symmetric, so the m2 dual is not a convex QP as claimed. Convexity of the m2 dual for a = +1 is therefore unestablished as written (it does hold for even kernels such as RBF, but only via a different argument, e.g., v^T Omega_s v = (1/2)(|s|^2 + <s, s'>) >= 0).

failure_location.quote: For $a = +1$ (even symmetry), $\Omega_s \succeq 0$ follows from the fact that $\Omega$ and $\Omega^*$ are individually PSD.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the a = +1 claim to even kernels (K(x, y) = K(-x, -y), e.g., RBF) or explicitly assume Omega_s PSD, and replace the false justification with a valid proof on that scope; the Section 10 guarantee claims then hold for the restricted class.
issues.overall_effect: The claims that m2 with a = +1 preserves P >= 0 and inherits the same SMO convergence and epsilon_tol-optimality guarantees (Section 10), and the abstract/conclusion statements that the same solver applies to m2, are unsupported for general kernels; in that regime Algorithm alg:smo loses its convexity-based guarantee for m2 inputs with a = +1.
issues.title: m2 (a = +1) PSD claim rests on a false premise and fails for general kernels
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a contained but nontrivial new PSD argument plus a scope restriction (even kernels or an explicit PSD hypothesis); the m2 a = +1 extension survives for the canonical kernels such as RBF, but the general-kernel claim is withdrawn and the stated proof must be replaced, which is more than minor yet avoids abandoning a substantive result.
